name: Islamic New Year
description: The first of Muharram opens a new year in the Islamic lunar calendar — a day for reflection and duʿāʾ.

name: ʿĀshūrāʾ — 10th of Muharram
description: Sunni Muslims mark it with fasting in remembrance of Allāh's relief of Mūsā; Shīʿa Muslims mourn the martyrdom of Imam al-Ḥusayn at Karbalāʾ. Observed differently by each tradition, with equal reverence.
disputed: Minority narrations place related events on 9 or 11 Muharram.

name: Arbaʿīn
description: Forty days after ʿĀshūrāʾ; Shīʿa Muslims mourn the martyrdom of Imam al-Ḥusayn, many undertaking pilgrimage to Karbalāʾ.
disputed: Some scholars compute the fortieth day as 17 Ṣafar.

name: Passing of the Prophet ﷺ
description: The Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ passed away on 28 Ṣafar in 11 AH (Shīʿa chronology; also cited in some Sunni histories).
disputed: Sunni majority chronology places the passing on 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal.

name: Mawlīd al-Nabī ﷺ
description: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ on 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal, marked by Sunni Muslims with recitation, charity and gatherings.
disputed: Date based on majority chronology; observance itself is a matter of scholarly difference.

name: Mawlīd al-Nabī ﷺ (Jaʿfarī)
description: Shīʿa Muslims of the Jaʿfarī school mark the Prophet's ﷺ birth on 17 Rabīʿ al-Awwal — the Prophet ﷺ and Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq share this birthday in this tradition.

name: Entry into Rajab
description: Rajab is one of the four sacred months in which warfare was traditionally prohibited.

name: Birthday of Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
description: Shīʿa Muslims celebrate the birth of Imam ʿAlī — uniquely born, in their tradition, inside the Kaʿba.

name: al-Isrāʾ wal-Miʿrāj
description: The Night Journey and Ascension, when the five daily prayers were ordained. Marked with night prayer and recitation.
disputed: The date is not established in the Qurʾān or strongest ḥadīths; 27 Rajab is the popular convention — many scholars discourage fixing it.

name: Birthday of Imam al-Ḥusayn
description: Birth of the Prophet's ﷺ grandson, honored across traditions; Shīʿa Muslims mark it with gatherings.

name: Mid-Shaʿbān (Niṣf Shaʿbān)
description: The middle night of Shaʿbān; some observe it with prayer and seeking forgiveness.
disputed: Its special status is disputed among scholars; Shīʿa Muslims also mark it as the birthday of Imam al-Mahdī.

name: First day of Ramaḍān
description: The month of fasting begins — subject to local moon sighting, so this date varies by region.

name: Martyrdom of Imam ʿAlī
description: Imam ʿAlī was struck by Ibn Muljam while praying at Kūfa, and passed away in this period.
disputed: Sources differ between 19 and 21 Ramaḍān for the strike and passing.

name: Laylat al-Qadr — search the odd nights
description: The Night of Power is sought in the odd nights of Ramaḍān's last ten; many traditions emphasize the 27th, but its exact night is deliberately unknown.
disputed: Never fix one date — the strongest guidance is to seek it across the odd nights.

name: Laylat al-Qadr (Shīʿa)
description: Shīʿa Muslims observe the nights of 19, 21 and 23 Ramaḍān as candidate Nights of Power, with the 23rd emphasized; the 21st also marks the martyrdom of Imam ʿAlī in these narrations.

name: ʿĪd al-Fiṭr
description: The festival of breaking the fast — Ṣalāt al-ʿĪd, zakāt al-fiṭr distributed beforehand, and celebration. Begins the evening the new moon is sighted.

name: Passing of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq
description: Imam al-Ṣādiq (d. 148 AH), eponym of the Jaʿfarī school of jurisprudence, passed away in Madīna.
disputed: Some sources give 25 Shawwāl, others 10 Rajab.

name: Yawm al-Tarwiyah
description: Pilgrims gather at Minā on the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, preparing for ʿArafah.

name: Yawm ʿArafah
description: The day of standing at ʿArafah — the climax of Ḥajj. Sunni Muslims not in Ḥajj commonly fast it.
disputed: Shīʿa tradition treats ʿArafah day as a ʿīd and discourages fasting it.

name: ʿĪd al-Aḍā
description: The festival of sacrifice, honoring Ibrāhīm's devotion — ṣalāh, sacrifice, and meat shared widely. Follows the Day of ʿArafah for most; for pilgrims, the rites of Minā.

name: Days of Tashrīq
description: The days following ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā spent at Minā during Ḥajj; days of eating, drinking and remembrance.

name: ʿĪd Ghadīr Khumm
description: Shīʿa Muslims mark the Prophet's ﷺ declaration at Ghadīr Khumm — 'whoever I am his mawlā, ʿAlī is his mawlā' — as the appointment of Imam ʿAlī. Sunni Muslims affirm the event at Ghadīr but understand the statement differently.

name: Ayyām al-Bīḍ — the White Days
description: Sunnah fasting on the 13th, 14th and 15th of every lunar month, when the moon is full.
